_comment: Fact ledger for resume-tailor's perspective-shift reframing (PLAN.md Phase 15, §9 2026-08-24). Each atom is a claim the master resume already makes: 'core' = what happened, 'invariants' = tokens (numbers/names) that MUST survive verbatim in any reframed rewrite, 'entities' = named tools/vendors/orgs allowed to appear (union with the master's own vocabulary forms factcheck.py's entity allowlist), 'claim_boundary' = the seniority/scope line a rewrite must not cross. 'source' pins the atom to the master so an editor can verify nothing was invented. This file is hand-authored and owner-reviewed -- resume-tailor reads it, never writes it. Atoms with source 'owner-confirmed <date>' are capabilities the owner confirmed directly rather than ones already written into the master; they are legal to use in a rewrite but must still respect their claim_boundary.

facts.core: 2+ years managing Vulnerability Management across cloud environments end-to-end, including fixing 2,800+ CVEs in OT Security within a year, working solo across a large attack surface
facts.claim_boundary: solo individual-contributor work across a large attack surface -- never 'led', 'managed a team of', 'architected', or implies more than 2 years

facts.core: works with protocols: IPsec, Kerberos, LDAP, Modbus, BACnet, EtherNet/IP, DNP3, PROFINET, SNMP
facts.claim_boundary: working knowledge of these protocols as used day-to-day -- never claim protocol design/authorship

facts.core: automated plugin development for OT security, cutting down manual repetitive work
facts.claim_boundary: automated own workflow -- not a platform/product the candidate owns or sells

facts.core: contributes to open-source security testing and development projects
facts.claim_boundary: contributor, not maintainer/owner of the upstream project (see holm-cloudsploit for the one project where 'upstream changes' is explicitly earned)

facts.core: at Holm Security AB, grew OT/SCADA CVE coverage from ~400 to 3,200+ within a year -- a 700% increase in the company's SCADA/OT security coverage for clients
facts.claim_boundary: solo IC contribution -- never 'led', 'owned the team', 'architected', or 'managed a group'

facts.core: worked across OT security products from Siemens, Schneider Electric, Rockwell Automation, ABB, Emerson, and Honeywell
facts.claim_boundary: product-level familiarity across six vendor families -- never claim a vendor certification/partnership that doesn't exist elsewhere on the resume

facts.core: managed the CloudSploit platform end-to-end across AWS, Azure, GCP, and Oracle, maintaining CIS benchmark compliance while maintaining upstream changes for the CloudSploit project
facts.claim_boundary: end-to-end ownership of one platform as a solo IC, with real upstream (open-source) contributions -- never 'built CloudSploit' or 'led a cloud security team'

facts.core: used Claude AI to automate security code development for vulnerability management and CloudSploit
facts.claim_boundary: AI-assisted own development workflow -- not an AI product built or shipped to others

facts.core: worked directly with clients to resolve issues and improve their experience with the company
facts.claim_boundary: individual technical point of contact -- never 'account management' or 'client relationship ownership'

facts.core: independently assessed Bill Manager (an e-commerce/billing app) and found: broken access control between user and admin roles, IDOR on invoices/billing records, privilege escalation via role/parameter tampering, SQL injection on login and search fields, stored/reflected XSS, insecure password reset flow, missing rate limiting on login attempts, and weak session/JWT handling
facts.claim_boundary: independent/personal assessment, not a paid client engagement or employer-sanctioned pentest

facts.core: documented findings and fixes through a GitHub Security Advisory on the Bill Manager project repository
facts.claim_boundary: responsible-disclosure documentation, not a CVE assignment unless the master says so elsewhere (it doesn't)

facts.core: completed hands-on labs on PortSwigger Web Security Academy across SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, authentication bypass, access control, SSRF, XXE, insecure deserialization, and API testing
facts.claim_boundary: self-paced training labs completed, not employer/client engagements

facts.core: practiced core Active Directory attack paths: Kerberoasting, LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning, pass-the-hash, and privilege escalation via misconfigured ACLs
facts.claim_boundary: personal-lab / self-study practice, not a client AD pentest engagement

facts.core: studying newer/advanced AD attack techniques: ADCS abuse (ESC1 to ESC8), delegation attacks (unconstrained, constrained, resource-based), Shadow Credentials, and BloodHound-driven attack path analysis
facts.claim_boundary: explicitly in-progress study, not claimed mastery -- keep the 'studying' framing, never present as completed expertise

facts.core: built a Subdomain & Attack Surface Enumeration Tool (Python, Requests, dnspython) that finds subdomains from public sources like crt.sh, brute-forces the rest locally with DNS lookups, scans open ports, and fingerprints the tech stack on each host using OpenVAS plus custom plugins
facts.claim_boundary: personal/independent project, not a commercial product

facts.core: maintains a custom fork of OpenVAS with custom NASL plugins for CVE checks the default feed doesn't cover yet, plus AI-automated scripts to keep the feed updated as new CVEs come out
facts.claim_boundary: personal fork/maintenance, not the official OpenVAS project

facts.core: built a real-world Active Directory home lab with a domain controller and client machines to practice AD attack paths (Kerberoasting, LLMNR poisoning, privilege escalation)
facts.claim_boundary: home lab for personal practice, not production infrastructure

facts.core: set up a home lab behind a pfSense firewall with intentionally vulnerable VMs (Metasploitable, DVWA, VulnHub) to practice scanning, exploiting, and the full pentesting flow
facts.claim_boundary: home lab for personal practice

facts.core: Offensive Security Certified Professional (OSCP), OffSec -- In Progress
facts.claim_boundary: in progress, never present as already certified

facts.core: completed TCM Security: Practical Ethical Hacking, Windows & Linux Privilege Escalation, OSINT Fundamentals, External Pentest Playbook
facts.claim_boundary: completed course certificates, not an industry-recognized cert like OSCP/CEH

facts.core: B.Tech Computer Science, Malla Reddy College of Engineering & Technology, Hyderabad, 2018-2022
entities: Malla Reddy College of Engineering & Technology
facts.claim_boundary: no CGPA/percentage is listed in the master and none may be invented (PLAN.md §9 2026-08-24: owner declined adding one)

facts.core: hands-on API security testing -- exercises authentication/authorization, BOLA/IDOR, injection and rate-limiting flaws against APIs using Burp Suite, Postman, crAPI and VAmPI
facts.claim_boundary: hands-on testing of APIs as an individual tester -- never API gateway/platform architecture, never 'owned the API security programme'

facts.core: performs secure code review and runs SAST/DAST tooling -- security-focused review of own and open-source code, including OpenVAS NASL plugins and CloudSploit upstream contributions
facts.claim_boundary: security-focused review and tooling on own and open-source code -- never 'owned the SAST programme', 'rolled out AppSec tooling enterprise-wide', or implies a dedicated AppSec team role

facts.core: works to and can speak to compliance frameworks: PCI-DSS, ISO 27001 and NIST CSF, alongside the CIS Benchmarks already enforced via CloudSploit
facts.claim_boundary: aligns work to these standards and can discuss them -- NOT an auditor, NOT a certification holder, never 'led the ISO 27001 audit' or 'certified'

facts.core: triages vulnerabilities end-to-end: CVSS-based severity scoring, false-positive analysis, risk-based prioritization, written remediation guidance, and re-validation after fixes -- the day-to-day method behind the Holm OT/SCADA CVE coverage work
facts.claim_boundary: solo IC triage across the OT and cloud surface -- never SLA/programme ownership, never 'defined the remediation SLA' or 'managed the vulnerability management programme for N clients'
